newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to undergo heart bypass operation-Interfax.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to undergo heart bypass operation-Interfax.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin will have a heart bypass operation at Moscow's Cardiological Centre, a senior Russian surgeon told Interfax news agency on Friday.
Professor Valery Sadrikov, deputy director of the Surgical Centre of the Academy of Medical Sciences, did not say when the operation would take place.

Sadrikov said the president would undergo "a shunt of the vessels which supply blood to the heart". This means a bypass in which a vein or an artery from the patient's leg or elsewhere is grafted in to divert blood around the blockage.
Yeltsin said on Thursday he would have a heart operation at the end of September.

He did not make clear what he was suffering from, however, referring only to "heart disease", and it was not clear until Friday whether the operation would be a fairly routine bypass procedure or a more serious treatment.
"The operation on the Russian president's heart will be carried out at the Cardiological Centre of Academician Chazov," Sadrikov told Interfax.

Yevgeny Chazov, a world-renowned specialist who kept Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev alive for almost a decade of hushed-up decline, confirmed that Yeltsin had undergone tests at his clinic, close to the president's apartment in a southwest Moscow suburb.
Apart from Chazov's and Sadrikov's centres, there are two others in Moscow which conduct heart bypass operations.
Yeltsin was twice hospitalised last year with ischaemic heart disease -- a reduction in the blood supply to the heart usually caused by a clogging of the cardiac arteries.

Doctor Alexander Myasnikov, who has worked at Chazov's centre for about 20 years, told Interfax such an operation lasts between five and seven hours during which the patient's heart is stopped and blood circulation is maintained artificially.
The best cardiosurgeons at the well-equipped Chazov centre are U.S.-trained, Maysnikov said.
